**Assignment**. Practice microbenchmarking your code to improve its performance
by exploring preallocation, vectorization, hash tables, and writing code in C++.

```{r define custom print for benchmark}
print.bench_mark <- function(x, ...) {
  out <- x[, c("expression", "median", "itr/sec", "mem_alloc")]
  class(out) <- setdiff(class(out), "bench_mark")
  print(out, ...)
  invisible(x)
}
```

**Vectorization vs. For Loop**: R is optimized for vectorized operations.
Repeatedly executing an operation in an R-level loop often adds overhead.
Practice this by squaring one million numbers in a for loop, preallocated for
loop, and with vectorization.

```{r}
x <- seq_len(1e6)

bench::mark(
  vectorized = x^2,

  preallocation = {
    result <- numeric(length(x))
    for (i in seq_along(x)) {
      result[i] <- x[i]^2
    }
    result
  },

  for_loop = {
    result <- numeric()
    for (i in seq_along(x)) {
      result[i] <- x[i]^2
    }
    result
  },

  check = TRUE,
  time_unit = "us"
)
```

**Counting for 10 Seconds**. How high can R count in 10 seconds? Write a while
loop and a C++ loop that counts for 10 seconds to show off some speed.

```{r while loop counting for 10 seconds}
r_count_until_time <- function(seconds) {
  seconds <- count <- 0
  start <- Sys.time()
  while (seconds < 10) {
    count <- count + 1
    end <- Sys.time()
    seconds <- as.numeric(difftime(end, start))
  }
  return(count)
}

r_count_until_time(10)
```


```{r cpp loop counting for 10 seconds}
Rcpp::cppFunction(
    '
    long long count_until_time(double seconds){
        using namespace std::chrono;
        long long count = 0;
        auto start = steady_clock::now();
        double elapsed = 0.0;

        while (elapsed < seconds){
            count++;
            auto now = steady_clock::now();
            elapsed = duration<double>(now - start).count();
        }

        return count;
    }',
    includes = "#include <chrono>"
)

count_until_time(10)
```

**Parallel Processing**. Use parallel processing to speed up a linear regression
that is fit to the mtcars dataset with a `Sys.sleep(1)` function to simulate an
expensive operation.

```{r}
predictors <- setdiff(names(mtcars), "mpg")

fit_model <- function(predictor) {
  formula <- reformulate(predictor, response = "mpg")
  Sys.sleep(1)
  lm(formula, data = mtcars) |>
    broom::tidy() |>
    dplyr::filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
    dplyr::mutate(predictor = predictor, .before = 1)
}

future::plan(future::multisession, workers = future::availableCores() - 1)


bench::mark(
  sequential = purrr::map(predictors, fit_model),
  parallel = furrr::future_map(predictors, fit_model),
  check = TRUE,
  time_unit = "s"
)
```
